newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty nervously drifts sideways, future hazy.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty nervously drifts sideways, future hazy.

text.p: The Polish zloty was virtually unchanged against the basket of currencies after drifting mainly sideways in nervous trade on Thursday.

Dealers said that the near-term outlook for the zloty was not clear, as the domestic market's slight dollar-selling sentiment was kept in check by expectations of a central bank intervention if the zloty gains more ground.

"The zloty can go either way on Friday, with the central bank's intervention barrier likely around three percent from parity if the local currency gains," said Piotr Czyzewski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 2.81/2.72 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Wednesday's 2.80/2.71 percent close.
It closed at 3.0020/50 to the dollar, up from 3.0040/60 on Wednesday and at 1.8175/90 to the mark, up from 1.8185/05.
Dealers said false rumours of central bank currency-buying interventions crippled trade for some time on Thursday and increased market caution when the zloty was drifting upwards.
Money market overnight and tomorrow/next rates closed flat at 21.95/22.15 percent as the market's regained balance after some tightness early in the week.
